title: Phantom Blade Zero Boss Guide - All Known Bosses & Strategies
description: Complete Phantom Blade Zero boss guide. All confirmed bosses from demos and trailers, with combat tips and strategies for each encounter.

sections.title: Boss Fights: What Is Established
sections.content:
This page covers how boss fights work in general. The roster - who the bosses are, where each was shown - lives on the boss list, and each fight has its own page recording its specific evidence.

What is established: S-GAME puts the count at 50 or more bosses, states that defeating a boss yields its weapon and its signature technique, and both are large numbers - 30-plus main weapons and 20-plus Phantom Edges - which is why the boss list doubles as the weapon list. Reviewers who finished the game report 50 to 55 hours for a full run. What is not established for any individual fight: weaknesses, resistances, phase counts and drops.

sections.title: Puppet Boss (String Puppet) - Demo Verified
sections.content:
The Puppet Boss was the first boss publicly demonstrated. This puppeteer-like opponent uses strings to control attacks from range while delivering swift melee strikes up close.

What The Footage Shows

  • String attacks - Ranged strings that sweep the arena, shown in the 4K demo.
  • Puppet summons - Smaller puppet enemies appear during the encounter; their spawn rules are not documented.
  • Close-range combos - Fast melee sequences at close range, per the same footage.

No weakness, phase count, drop or timing data has been published for this fight. The mechanics above are what S-GAME chose to show publicly; anything beyond that is inference, and there is a full strategy-free record on the boss page.

sections.title: Huangxing — Demo Verified
sections.content:
Huangxing is an aggressive warrior boss featured in the 4K Demo. Known for relentless pressure and powerful sword techniques.

The director described this boss as somewhat Soulslike at the middle difficulty, which in context means predictable, learnable combos rather than adaptive behaviour. No weakness, phase or drop data is published; details on the boss page.

sections.title: How The Mechanics Apply To Boss Fights
sections.content:
No move-by-move strategy is published for any boss before release, so this section is limited to what the ported combat data actually supports. Each line links to the page it comes from.

  • Draining the enemy's Sha-chi is the opening. Normal attacks cannot reduce an enemy's bar; Sha-chi attacks and making them block can. When a bar empties that side is guard-broken, takes extra damage and cannot block. Details: combat.
  • Telegraph colours decide the answer, not the boss. White-glow attacks can be precisely guarded; red-glow attacks cannot be blocked and want a precise dodge; both feed Ghost Step, which moves you behind the enemy where the follow-up cannot be blocked. Black-glow costs an enormous amount of Sha-chi to block. This is why coverage keeps reducing the game to "master parry timing".
  • Switching weapons is a resource reset, not just a damage change. The community combat write-up describes the swap refilling the Sha-chi bar and clearing guard break, at the cost of a cooldown on the weapon you swapped out. Carrying two main weapons with different profiles is therefore a defensive option as much as an offensive one.
  • You cannot grind past a wall. There is no XP system; growth comes from equipment, found collectibles and weapon upgrades, and defeated enemies do not simply repopulate when you rest. If a boss stops you, the intended answer is a different loadout, not a detour to level up.
  • Bells are the rest point. They clear map fog, restore combat resources and fast-travel - and in 66 Days they are the only save. Outside that mode, dying does not advance any day counter; the 66-day clock belongs to that mode alone.

What reviewers say to expect from the fights themselves: the praise is consistent - "truly spectacular" (Saudi Gamer, 100), bosses that "burst with invention" (Areajugones, 95) - and so is one criticism, that boss pacing can feel like taking turns (Eurogamer, 6/10) and that some fights run long (Critical Hits, leaked pre-embargo). Full scores on the reviews page.

sections.title: What changed this week
sections.content:
The director stated in October that the game has at least 50 bosses, and that the count tracks the weapon count because defeating a boss is how its weapon is earned. The boss list is therefore the closest thing to a weapon list.

A boss called The Hunt was shown in IGN footage on 13 October - the assassin Soul fights on the moving cart in the opening, here as a full encounter. What it drops has not been announced.

26-27 October: the review wave arrived, which put the first outside numbers on length (50 and 55 hours) and the first real criticism of boss pacing. The strategy advice above was rewritten at the same time: the previous version told readers to "level up elsewhere" when stuck and warned that death advances a 66-day timer. Both were wrong - there is no XP system, and the day counter exists only in 66 Days mode.
